short: The prince who made Gwynedd the dominant power in Wales for forty years.
full:
Llywelyn ab Iorwerth had taken control of Gwynedd by 1199 and spent four decades turning a patchwork of Welsh kingdoms into something close to a single principality under his leadership. He married Joan, an illegitimate daughter of King John, which did not prevent John from invading in 1211 and briefly reducing him to the far west.

He recovered within two years by allying with the English barons in revolt, and Welsh grievances were written into Magna Carta. In 1216 he held a council at Aberdyfi at which the other Welsh rulers did homage to him, an arrangement the English crown accepted at the Peace of Worcester in 1218. He styled himself Prince of Aberffraw and Lord of Snowdon rather than Prince of Wales, but the substance was there. He died a monk at Aberconwy in April 1240, and his settlement collapsed under his son within four years.
